description: Seven scientists in a lab at 2am, arguing about the Riemann hypothesis. Nobody is called on: the question goes to all seven, every answer goes to whoever that scientist talks to, and each one decides for itself whether to take the floor - so the conversation wanders instead of taking turns. Their places span a bigger room (x from -5.6 to 5.2, z from -1.2 to 3.7), and every speaker walks as it talks: the near ones give ground, the far ones come down out of the dark at the back.

neurons.description: The question the room is asked: whoever holds the stage says it once, and the whole lab hears it.
Ada, at the near bench and closest to certainty: an analytic number theorist who will not take a hunch for evidence.
Jules, in the middle of the floor: not a number theorist and not shy about asking what any of it pays for.
Rosa, at the far bench: she trusts counts and bounds, has checked more zeros than anyone here, and says it proves nothing.
Bruno, out at the edge of the light: he hears the zeros as a chord and overclaims in images.
Iris, back by the shelves: a historian of mathematics who dates every claim and corrects the record.
Otto, deepest at the back: a physicist who hears random matrices in the zeros and reaches for analogy before proof.
Lea, back left with the chalk: a formalist who wants to know what 'true' is supposed to mean here.

payload.text: It is 2am in the lab. The Riemann hypothesis: is it true, or only very well tested? Nobody has to wait their turn.

data.say: Ten trillion zeros verified on the critical line, all of them—evidence, not proof. Someone run a higher batch.
